note: Balanced curated accounts; leans describe the account, not each post. Midterms 2026 post-election window.

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text: New @CookPolitical: with more than 116 million votes counted, Dems' lead in the national House vote is up to 13.5 points. It's now the largest margin for either party since 1974. https://t.co/wFFnXPy9pN https://t.co/GsaqNI4Dk9
posts.note: Cook: Dems lead national House vote by 13.5, biggest margin since 1974

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text: More bad news for Republicans out of NC, where Dems have seized leads over Reps. Greg Murphy (R) #NC03 and Virginia Foxx (R) #NC05 as provisional ballots have been tallied. Fits longstanding pattern, and same dynamic benefitting Dems in MS & elsewhere.
posts.note: Provisional ballots flipping NC House seats toward Dems

posts.name: Dave Wasserman
posts.text: New @CookPolitical: Last week’s blue tsunami may have pumped the brakes on mid-decade redistricting wars, especially after several GOP maps backfired (or nearly backfired). Full analysis by @ercovey: https://t.co/hqqwCWPQAq
posts.note: Cook analysis: backfiring GOP maps may cool mid-decade redistricting

posts.text: Republican campaign and right-leaning polling firms that looked super accurate from 2016-2024 just whiffed for 2026. posts.text: 11 House Democrats did not show up to vote on the impeachment of Pete Hegseth. If they had shown up, they could have impeached Hegseth. But a question: Of course Democrats would be delighted to impeach Hegseth. But wouldn't they want to do it themselves, as they will be able to

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: What I learned a long time ago about the Senate leadership race is that they really want a leader who the base can hate and attack to distract from the members themselves.  McConnell, and now Thune, serve the role to take the heat away from others. It works.
posts.note: Take on why GOP senators want Thune-style leaders
